items.title: Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.quote: an audit log of changes to system prompts or other model configuration (including prompts) that affect the underlying working of the systems
items.why: Source of the quotation (provision 8.3, a 'should', addressed to developers). Provision 6.1: developers and operators shall evaluate access control frameworks and secure APIs, models, data and pipelines. 6.3: dedicated environments with least privilege. 12.1: operators shall log system and user actions. 7.4: operators shall tell end-users before models are updated. Voluntary.

items.title: ETSI TS 104 223 V1.1.1: Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Baseline Cyber Security Requirements for AI Models and Systems
items.quote: identify appropriate measures to secure APIs, models, data, and training and processing pipelines
items.why: The international specification carrying the same access control and audit log provisions as the UK Code. A specification, not law.

items.title: Guidelines for secure AI system development: Secure deployment
items.locator: Sections 'Secure your infrastructure' and 'Protect your model continuously'
items.quote: You apply appropriate access controls to your APIs, models and data, and to their training and processing pipelines
items.why: Says access control applies in research and development as well as in deployment, and warns that attackers may tamper with models, data or prompts during or after training. Guidance, not a rule.

items.title: Guidelines for secure AI system development: Secure development
items.locator: Section 'Identify, track and protect your assets'
items.quote: You have processes and tools to track, authenticate, version control and secure your assets
items.why: Lists the assets that count: models, data, prompts, software, documentation and logs, and says logs themselves are sensitive. Basis for treating a prompt as an asset under version control.

items.title: UK GDPR, Article 32: Security of processing
items.quote: who has access to personal data does not process them except on instructions from the controller
items.why: The binding rule where personal data is involved: security appropriate to the risk, including the risk of unauthorised alteration or access, and a duty to ensure people with access act only on instructions. Not specific to AI and silent on prompts and models as such.

items.title: Cyber Essentials: Requirements for IT infrastructure v3.2
items.quote: Your organisation must be in control of your user accounts and the access privileges that allow access to your organisational data and services.
items.why: The government-backed baseline: accounts only for authorised individuals, unique credentials, and special care with administrative accounts. Not written for AI, but the platforms on which prompts and models are edited are ordinary accounts within its scope. Certification is voluntary.

items.title: Implementation Guide for the AI Cyber Security Code of Practice
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.locator: Provision 5.4, PDF p. 27, 'Implement Strong Data Access Controls'
items.quote: Programmatic updates via pipelines have strict RBAC and approvals in place to prevent abuse.
items.why: The only source read that speaks of approval before a change lands, and only for automated pipeline updates. Explanatory, not a requirement.

items.title: Poisoning Attacks on LLMs Require a Near-constant Number of Poison Samples
items.locator: Abstract on the AI Security Institute research page
items.quote: 250 poisoned documents similarly compromise models across all model and dataset sizes
items.why: Source of the figure. Models from 600 million to 13 billion parameters; the same dynamics were shown for fine-tuning. Why control over who can add to training and fine-tuning data matters: the number of documents needed does not grow with the model. Only the abstract on the Institute's page was read.

items.title: LLM07:2025 System Prompt Leakage
items.quote: the system prompt should not be considered a secret, nor should it be used as a security control
items.why: Warns against putting credentials or permission rules in a prompt: access must be enforced outside the model. Community consensus document, not a standard. No publication date is shown on the page.

items.title: Guidance on AI and data protection: How should we assess security and data minimisation in AI?
items.locator: Section 'How should we ensure training data is secure?'
items.quote: Your technical teams should record and document all movements and storing of personal data from one location to another.
items.why: The data protection regulator on audit trails for training data. The page carries a banner that the guidance is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act.
